· The wiring was renewed last month; sound.
· The earth pin on the amp’s plug has been freshly cut; inside the amp, a red jumper wire connecting the chassis to the microphone stand. Reggie Holloway’s fingerprints on the wire’s clips.
· The stage circuit’s residual current protection was switched off by hand at the panel at 17.58 and back on at 18.06. Only the manager has the panel key.
The amp had been serviced three weeks earlier.

His prints are on the jumper wire; the protection circuit was switched off at a panel only he has a key to, six minutes before the death, and back on two minutes after. Mavis had found the Lakeshore cash and asked him about it.

She knew. She was going in the morning; Lakeshore’s men would have killed me, then her. I cut the amp’s earth and wired it to the stand. At the panel I switched the protection off, then on. So it’d look like an accident. They said it takes one second.

On the evening of 23 August 2030, at a blues club in the South Side, during a sound check, the club’s owner Mavis Holloway (68) collapsed on stage on touching the microphone stand; she died in the ambulance.

Present in the club: manager Reggie Holloway, guitarist Cedric Banks, singer Tasha Monroe, bartender Earline Pope. The building owner Vic Romano had left the club ten minutes before the incident.

The bartender gave Mavis’s last words and the corridor camera, the singer what happened on stage. The electrical line showed the prints on the jumper wire and the panel, the till line the Lakeshore cash. The guitarist’s line only cleared the amp.
An old building can be the excuse for anything. First look at what was renewed most recently.

Club manager Reggie Holloway was running Lakeshore Freight’s cash through his aunt’s club. When Mavis Holloway found the money and said she would go to bube in the morning, Reggie cut the earth on the guitarist’s amp, made the microphone stand live with a jumper wire, and switched off the protection circuit at the panel before the sound check.
